newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Brit Gas Q2 seen around break-even.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Brit Gas Q2 seen around break-even.

text.p: Tough competition in the industrial supply market will have kept British Gas's results near the break-even level in its traditionally weak second quarter, analysts said.

Their forecasts for net historic results range from a 30 million loss to a 40 million profit, compared with a 30 million profit in the same 1995 period. The interim dividend is expected unchanged at 6.4 pence per share.
But the results, due Thursday, are of no major concern, analysts said. Regulatory wrangles, demerger plans and contract negotiations with gas producers are seen as far more important.
"The results are pretty much a side issue," said Daniel Martin at Barclay de Zoete Wedd.
Featuring centre stage instead is the industry regulator's price review of British Gas' pipeline unit TransCo.
The main question here is whether British Gas will reject the regulator's final price proposals and request the matter tbe referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC).

The proposals came out in August and British Gas has until October 7 to decide whether to accept them. The pricing plans are considered harsh and are expected to lead to considerable dividend cuts if implemented, analysts said.
A referral may well bring concessions, but several analysts said an MMC investigation would be time consuming.

They added the company can gain more by focusing its management efforts on its break-up plan and its talks to alter the long-term take-or-pay contracts, which oblige it to buy gas from producers even if it cannot find a market.
"I expect them (British Gas) to go for a referral, but that would be the wrong course," said one analyst who declined to be named. "There are bigger issues to address."

British Gas aims to have shareholders vote on its planned demerger some time early next year. The company wants to split itself into a trading business and a separate firm which will own the storage and distribution network.

While the demerger is being prepared, British Gas is also trying to sweeten the take-or-pay contracts. The company has been tightlipped so far on the subject, although it expects to announce a breakthrough by the end of the year.
Analysts, meanwhile, hope they won't have wait much longer following recent rumours that a deal with a major gas producer is near.
